chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and others, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from ʿAlī ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, can any part of a carcass be benefited from? He said: “No.”

I said: It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم passed by a dead sheep and said: “What would have been upon the people of this sheep, if they did not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its hide?” He said: “That was a sheep belonging to Sawdah bint Zamʿah, the wife of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and it was a lean sheep whose meat was not benefited from, so they left it until it died. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘What would have been upon its people, if they did not benefit from its meat, to benefit from its hide’—that is, that it be slaughtered properly.”

key_terms.الْمَيْتَةُ: a carcass; an animal that died without proper slaughter
key_terms.تُذَكَّى: to be properly slaughtered according to sacred law
key_terms.يُنْتَفَعُ: to derive benefit or use from something

ai.seo_question: Can any part of a dead animal be used, and how is the hadith about the sheep's hide understood?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling regarding benefiting from a carcass and clarifies a reported statement of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم about a sheep's hide. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains that the report refers to the animal being properly slaughtered, not to permissibility of benefiting from the hide of an unslaughtered carcass.
